newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH IND SALES UP, WAGES BIGGER PROBLEM - ANALYSTS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH IND SALES UP, WAGES BIGGER PROBLEM - ANALYSTS.

text.p: Czech real industrial sales surged by 10.1 percent year-on-year in April but analysts said it would be premature to predict a sustained upturn and warned that industrial wage growth was a more serious consideration.

Preliminary data released on Thursday by the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) suggested that April was the first month this year to show positive growth in industry -- in March industrial sales fell 0.8 percent -- but nominal wages grew by 14.7 percent after 14.6 percent in the previous month.
"As concerns industrial sales definitely each figure which might suggest a change in the downtrend is good news," said Jindrich Weiss of Zivnostenska Banka.

The figures come a day after the government announced a new economic strategy, promising tighter fiscal policy, a freeze on public sector pay, and negotiations with unions to restrain wage growth in the private sector.

Czech retail price inflation was 6.7 percent in April but a sharp depreciation of the crown this week -- by nearly 10 percent versus the dollar and mark -- has revived fears of a resurgance of inflation.
Rob van de Wijngaert, an economist at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, said Thursday's industrial wage figures were a timely indication of how difficult the government's task would be.
"Basically the Czechs live beyond their means so still with such high wages it doesn't show any readiness by the Czech workers to accept wage cuts in the future," he said.
The CSU said that the figures had been affected by the presence of one extra working day in April this year versus April 1996.

Analysts said this had exaggerated the strength of Czech industry in April although they said the figures may indicate that some of the darker predictions about the Czech economy over the last few weeks may have been overstated.

"At the very beginning of the year most of the anlaysts were very optimistic, then the picture darkened probably too much...definitely it might be better than it looked several weeks ago but we will have to watch the trend closely," said Weiss.

The CSU said that the main impetus behind April's industrial sales growth was transport - which grew by 44.2 percent. The rubber and plastic industry was the second fastest growth area, rising 21.3 percent and the paper and polygraphic sector saw sales jump by 19.2 percent.
Overall, in the first four months of 1997, the CSU data showed real industrial sales rising by 1.4 percent year-on-year after falling 1.5 percent in the first quarter.
The Czech economic slowdown has been exacerbated by high interest rates which were recently raised further to protect the crown from a speculative assault from abroad.

On Monday, the Czech National Bank gave up its battle to support the crown at levels then prevailing -- around 18 to the mark compared with 19.5 on Thursday -- but raised the discount rate to 13.0 percent from 10.5 to restrain the extent of the currency's decline.
